_note: Week-by-week baby size/development/symptoms/tips, weeks 4-40. Sizes and measurements are widely-cited approximations, not a diagnostic measurement — every baby grows differently.
disclaimer: This guide is general information, not medical advice. Always follow your own doctor's guidance for your pregnancy.

weeks.development: The fertilized egg has implanted in the uterus, and the basic layers that will form your baby are starting to develop.
tips: Start a prenatal vitamin with folic acid if you haven't already.
Rest when you're tired — feeling more tired than usual is normal now.
Try small, frequent meals if nausea is an issue.

weeks.development: Your baby can make facial expressions, and the neck is more defined.
common_symptoms: More energy than the first trimester
Skin changes, like a dark line down the belly
tips: Keep up gentle activity your doctor has approved, like walking.
Comfortable, supportive shoes help as your balance shifts.
This is a good time to start thinking about your hospital bag and birth plan basics.

weeks.development: Your baby can blink, and eyelashes have grown in.
common_symptoms: Swelling in the feet and ankles
Needing to pee more often again
tips: Many doctors recommend sleeping on your side in the third trimester.
Packing your hospital bag a few weeks before your due date can ease last-minute stress.
Keep track of your baby's movements, and mention any big change in pattern to your doctor.
weeks.review_note: Side-sleeping is widely recommended, but exact guidance (which side, from which week) varies — good to confirm with her doctor.
